findings.title: Admin group add_members/remove_member read :group_id but the router only sets :id
findings.body: The new routes `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` are declared at the top level of `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new do ... end` (i.e., not inside a `collection do` block), so Rails generates them as MEMBER routes `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members`. The corresponding JS (`Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json', ...)`) matches those URLs, so the param that holds the group id is `params[:id]`. However, both new actions read the group with `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` (line 66 for add_members, line 85 for remove_member). Because `params[:group_id]` is never populated by the router, every real PUT/DELETE from the admin UI will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` and the add/remove member functionality will be completely broken in production. The controller specs pass because RSpec controller specs bypass routing and inject `group_id:` directly into the params hash, which is exactly the test gap that hides this bug. Either change the actions to read `params[:id]`/`params.require(:id)`, or add a `:group_id` segment to the routes.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` returns `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For any group whose member count is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 users with the default 50/page, or 100 users, etc.) this evaluates to one more page than actually exists. As a result `showingLast` stays false on the real last page and the "next" control is rendered enabled. Clicking it then sends `findMembers` with an `offset` that is clamped to `user_count` by `Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`, so the server returns zero rows and the user lands on an empty trailing page that the pagination arrows can never get them back out of. The intended formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: addMembers never clears usernames and never reports errors
findings.body: The action body just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` and ignores the returned promise. The `// TODO: should clear the input` comment acknowledges the problem: after a successful add, the user-selector still contains the same text, so a second click re-submits the same usernames (silently de-duplicated server-side but still wasteful and confusing). Because no `.then`/`.catch` is wired up either, any failure from the underlying PUT (e.g. the parameter bug described above, or a validation error) is swallowed: the spinner clears, the input keeps the value, and the admin gets no feedback at all. The input should be cleared on success and any error should be surfaced.

findings.title: add_members splits usernames on comma without trimming or rejecting blanks
findings.body: `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username)` is called verbatim on each substring. If the user-selector ever produces a name with surrounding whitespace (e.g. `"alice , bob"` or stray trailing whitespace from an autocomplete suggestion), `User.find_by_username(" alice ")` returns nil and the entry is silently dropped — the request still returns `success_json`, the admin sees "added" and no user was actually added. The code should also explicitly skip blank entries instead of relying on `find_by_username("")` returning nil. Similar trimming is performed in other parts of the app (e.g. user creation) and would be expected here.

findings.title: Stray closing inside {{#each}} block produces malformed HTML
findings.body:
Inside `{{#each m in members}}` there is a literal `` on line 19 with no matching opening `
`, all of which sits inside a ``/`` structure. This is leftover from a previous container-based layout that survived the model refactor. Browsers will auto-correct the DOM in inconsistent ways and it is invalid markup, so any tooling that relies on the parse tree (a11y, sanitizers, etc.) can be confused. The `` should be removed.

findings.title: save error handler crashes on non-JSON error responses
findings.body: On failure the controller does `var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors;`. If the server returns a non-JSON body (e.g. an HTML 500 page from an unhandled exception, a maintenance page, or an empty body for a network failure), `$.parseJSON` throws a `SyntaxError`. That throw is swallowed by the promise chain, `disableSave` is reset to false in `.finally`, and the admin sees no error message at all — the save button just becomes clickable again with no indication that anything went wrong. The handler should guard against parse failure (try/catch or typeof check) and fall back to a generic error or `e.responseText` itself.

findings.title: add_members/remove_member specs use group_id but production only exposes :id
findings.body: Every new spec for the two actions passes the group identifier as `group_id:` (lines 94, 103, 115, 125). RSpec controller specs bypass Rails routing and inject that key directly into `params`, so the controller's `params.require(:group_id)` succeeds and the tests pass. In production the routes (`put "members"`/`delete "members"` under `resources :groups, constraints: AdminConstraint.new`) are member routes that expose the group id as `:id`, not `:group_id`, so the same actions will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` for every real request. Either rewrite the specs as request/integration specs that actually go through the router, or pass the param as `id: group.id` (and have the controller read `params[:id]`) so that the suite exercises the real contract. The `cannot remove members from automatic groups` example also uses `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route only accepts DELETE for that action — that mismatch is similarly masked by the controller-spec scope.
